topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Increasing Sizes
explanation: The memory hierarchy is a tiered storage structure designed to minimize memory access latency by bridging the speed mismatch between the CPU and main memory (DRAM). It consists of progressively larger cache levels (L1, L2, L3) organized such that capacity increases, access time increases, and cost per bit decreases at each subsequent level. Caching strategies exploit the principle of locality (temporal and spatial) by moving frequently referenced data into the faster, smaller levels closest to the processor. This organization effectively reduces the average memory access time (AMAT) to optimize overall system throughput.
